_doc: Source of truth for Ultrastable's positioning and memory rule. Prose elsewhere is generated or checked against this file: `python3 -m foundation doctrine --apply` injects the line into the markdown files listed under `inject`, `--check` (run by checks.yml and the tests) fails when any listed file lacks it or states a contradiction, and gaplint rules GL008 and GL009 read this file. The `autonomy` block carries the autonomy line, injected and checked like the tagline. `banned_framing` is checked across every tracked text file and every commit message. Changed only by a reviewed PR.
tagline: Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

licensing.decision: 2026-11-11 (Rowan): no patent. Source-available hybrid license: free for non-commercial use, a Commercial License with revenue share for any commercial use. Specs live in ultrastable/spec and replace the patent drafts; the patent drafts are archived in ip/.
required_patterns: COMMERCIAL USE REQUIRES A COMMERCIAL LICENSE

memory.rule: Code is the only memory. All project state lives in this repository (docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.md and data files). No agent relies on chat, tool or platform memory; a thread is never the only record.

runs_on_itself._doc: Self-reference is the proof. Ultrastable runs its own planning, issues, managers, trust ledger, plussing budget, specs, release and reporting with the code it gives everyone else. `python3 -m foundation selfhost --verify` fails when any of it depends on a tool with no recorded adapter; `foundation doctrine --check` runs that verifier and fails when a listed file lacks the line.
runs_on_itself.line: Ultrastable runs on itself: its roadmap, issues, managers, trust ledger, plussing budget and specs are run by the same code it gives everyone else, from this repository alone, with any tools (`python3 -m foundation selfhost`).
contradictions: ultrastable (does not|doesn't|will not|won't) run on itself
runs_on_itself._public_note: Public and SAFE NOW files carry only the short tagline, never the mechanism line; they are check_only and edited by hand.

loops_thesis: Vibe coding is a start, not a system. A system is many agents with separate duties, running code loops that check, report and improve themselves. Ultrastable is built that way: multi-agent, self-referential loops, not a prompt and not a single code agent.

autonomy._doc: Autonomy is self-referential loops plus the ability to close them. Knowing without being able to act is useless, so the system is privileged to close its own loops. Injected after the tagline into the md_files of `inject`; the short tagline alone goes in the public check_only files. The loop registry and its verifier (`python3 -m foundation loops --verify`) make it testable.
autonomy.tagline: A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them.
autonomy.line: A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them. Knowing without being able to act is useless, so the system is privileged to close its own loops (`python3 -m foundation loops --verify`).

creation_destruction._doc: The vision behind the name (owner, 2026-11-12). An ultrastable system (Ashby, 1952) keeps a small set of essential variables inside limits and, when one leaves them, changes its own structure until they return. So the system is free to create and destroy anything that is its own: code, config, workers, loops, doctrine, whole components. The owner's image is the dance of creation and destruction; it stays in this note and out of product copy, because a living religion's deity is not a brand asset. Complete control is granted inside a boundary and the boundary is what makes that grant safe: it is a mechanism, never a slogan. `boundary.status` says what is true today and `foundation doctrine --check` fails when the claim outruns the mechanism (status `enforced` with no runtime definition). Injected and checked like the autonomy line.
creation_destruction.tagline: Ultrastable creates and destroys its own parts to stay stable.
creation_destruction.line: Ultrastable creates and destroys its own parts to stay stable: inside its boundary the system has complete control to build, replace, delete and rebuild itself, and the boundary, not a permission prompt, keeps a failure from reaching anything outside it (`python3 -m foundation doctrine --check`).

essential_variables._doc: What must stay inside limits while everything else may change. These are the existing limits, named once; this block adds none and removes none.

boundary._doc: `declared`: the boundary is policy (branches, previews, backups, the interrupt gate, standing limits) and the system runs on hosts that also hold things that are not its own. `enforced`: a runtime definition at `definition` confines the system so that destroying the whole container loses nothing outside it. Move to `enforced` only in the PR that adds the definition and its test.

self_bootstrapped._doc: The doctrine is bootstrapped by the system itself: its own principles, self-reference, autonomy and self-improvement loops. That is all that is said about its origin. The kernel is doctrine/kernel-8.2.1.md.

banned_framing._doc: Fails when a tracked text file or a commit message compares the doctrine with an external rule-set approach. The pattern is assembled in foundation/doctrine.py from fragments so this repository never states it; this block lists only the exclusions.

stability_line: Ultra-stable: infrastructure that works so nobody notices.

zero_fuss.rule: Zero-fuss, super-simple, zero-knowledge setup. A user with no technical knowledge can get a working result with no keys, config files, installs, hosting or jargon to handle.
